segments.text: you asked why i watched the midnight train though no one steps down for me
sit here stranger out of the rain i'll tell you what i used to be i was 17 with a paper
mile path away and a borrowed coat i left my mother beside this track with her warning
caught in my throat I carried crates by the harbor wall played piano in rooms without names
loved one woman through spring and fall then traded our peace for brighter flames
she left one note by an empty cup you chase every door that appears I laughed pack light and hurried
up that laugh costs 20 years so hear me stranger hear me plain a life is more than believing
every window upon a train shows what the arc was not seeing i won some gold i lost some friends
i learned too late what time can stand if somebody waits when your journey ends
Go home, go home to there
The stranger turned beneath the station light
My own young face stared back
Same paper map, same lies, too bright
Same one-way ticket on the track
I seized his sleeve as the whistle cried
But my hand passed through like steam
Does she forgive me?
The boy replied, I said
wake up before i dream hear me stranger hear me now let find this one departure turn from the
engine keep your power love is the longer adventure the train rolled over the silver
And the boy walked out of view
I stayed on on platform three
Then rose to go home too
If her old lamp still warms the pain
I'll knock and speak my name
No more stories for the midnight train
I'm going home
The way I can
